data.text:
The Philippines is opening up a key gateway for global internet traffic—one that could finally chip away at slow speeds and high costs.

The Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) has signed telecommunications firm InfiniVAN to develop the Poro Point Cable Landing Station in La Union into an open gateway for international submarine cables, a move expected to expand internet capacity, improve network reliability, and help bring down connectivity costs for Filipino businesses and households.

The shift to an “open” cable landing station signals a push to ease long-standing bottlenecks in the country’s internet ecosystem, where limited gateways have kept bandwidth expensive and unevenly distributed.

The agreement, signed on March 12, covers the Poro Point facility under the Luzon Bypass Infrastructure, a 240-kilometer fiber corridor linking Baler, Aurora to San Fernando, La Union.

By allowing multiple submarine cable operators and local providers to connect through the same facility, the setup is expected to drive competition and improve how data moves across the country.

data.text:
Pormal na nagkaisa ang Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) at TXTFIRE Philippines para sa mas mabilis at mas epektibong pagtugon sa sunog at sakuna sa Metro Manila.

Sa Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) na pinirmahan ni MMDA Chairman Atty. Don Artes at TXTFIRE PHILIPPINES Executive Director Royce Gerik Chua, nilalaman nito ang kanilang partnership para sa: 

🚨 mas mahusay na koordinasyon sa panahon ng emerhensiya,
🚨  cross-training sa pagitan ng mga tumutugon sa sunog at sakuna,
🚨   pagbabahagi ng kaalaman sa paggamit ng equipment at resources para sa mas maayos na pagtugon sa sakuna

Lumagda rin sa MOA sina Pateros Mayor Gerald German at Parañaque Mayor Edwin Olivarez bilang saksi sa naganap na kasunduan. 
#MMDA #mmdaatyourservice
